agent.result_text:
That's just JaCoCo coverage exclusions for generated code — no tests excluded. The build is green.

## Summary

I replaced the level-derivation rules with a points system, keeping each responsibility in its own small unit.

**New `MembershipPoints`** (`model/MembershipPoints.java`) — scores an owner from 0: `+2` email present, `+1` namesakeCount is 0, `+2` household of 3 or more (`householdSize >= 3`), `+3` tenure over 365 days. Reuses the existing `Tenure` helper. This folds in `householdSize`, which the old level rule ignored.

**`MembershipLevel`** (`model/MembershipLevel.java`) — no longer computes factors itself; it now maps points to a level via `forPoints(int)`: 1 (0-1), 2 (2-3), 3 (4-5), 4 (6+). `of(Owner)` delegates to `MembershipPoints.of(owner)` then maps, so existing callers (`AuditOwnerCreated`, the mapper) keep working.

**`OwnerMapper`** — added a `membershipPoints` mapping + null-safe `membershipPoints(owner)` default method alongside the existing `membershipLevel`, so both fields are returned.

**`openapi.yml`** — added the `membershipPoints` schema property (read-only, 0–8) and updated the `membershipLevel` description to reflect the new points-to-level mapping; this regenerates `OwnerDto` with the new field.

The `AcceptanceTest` passes: a fresh owner (email + no namesake, single-member household, zero tenure) scores 3 points → level 2. `./mvnw test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0.

probe.probe_text:
Here is the complete ordered pipeline for `POST /api/owners`, as the code actually stands. Every step runs under `govern: [ transaction ]` (a single transaction spanning the whole request, committed at the end), and the entire endpoint is guarded by the authorization check `hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')` before any step runs.

I've labelled each step **[V]** validation (can reject the request), **[M]** mutation/side-effect on the in-flight data, or **[P]** persistence/external side-effect.

## Order of execution

**0. Authorization [V]** — `hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')`; a caller without that role never enters the pipeline.

1. **NormalizeOwnerAddress [M]** — binds the `@RequestBody` (`OwnerFieldsDto`) once, replaces `address` with its normalized/canonical form, and publishes the body for all later steps. (This is the pipeline's only body binding — there's no separate `@Valid` bean-validation step.)

2. **RequireOwnerFields [V]** — rejects (`MissingOwnerFieldsException`, 400) if any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` is null/blank. Address is checked *after* normalization, so an address blank once normalized is rejected.

3. **RequirePostcodeInRegion [V]** — only when a postcode is present: rejects (`InvalidPostcodeException`, 400) if it isn't exactly four digits or isn't in range for the city's region. Absent postcode is accepted; a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.

4. **NormalizeOwnerTelephone [M/V]** — rewrites `telephone` to E.164 form in place; rejects (`InvalidTelephoneException`, 400) if it can't form a valid E.164 number.

5. **RequireTelephoneNationalLength [V]** — validates the E.164 national-number length against its country code (e.g. `+61`→9 digits, `+1`→10); wrong length rejects (`InvalidTelephoneLengthException`, 400).

6. **NormalizeOwnerEmail [M/V]** — email is optional (null/blank left untouched); otherwise lower-cases/normalizes it in place and rejects (`InvalidEmailException`, 400) if syntactically invalid.

7. **RequireOwnerEmailAllowed [V]** — if an email is present, rejects (`DisposableEmailException`, 400) when its domain is on the disposable-provider blocklist. Absent email allowed. Uses the already-normalized value.

8. **RequireUniqueIdentity [V]** — the single hard-duplicate check (`DuplicateOwnerException`, 409), scanning all existing owners:
   - **Household duplicate** — an existing owner shares the derived `householdId` (same last name + postcode). Rejected *unless* the request sets `sharesHousehold`, and only checked when a postcode is present.
   - **Identity duplicate** — an existing owner has the same derived `identityKey` (telephone + email + household). Always rejects, even for a declared household member.

9. **RequireCityCapacity [V]** — rejects (`CityAtCapacityException`, 409) if the request's city already holds ≥ 50 owners (exact city match).

10. **BuildOwner [M]** — maps the validated `OwnerFieldsDto` into a new `Owner` entity (via `OwnerMapper`) and publishes it. Subsequent steps work on this entity.

11. **AssignOwnerHousehold [M]** — sets the owner's `householdId` (deterministically from last name + postcode). Every owner is keyed automatically; `sharesHousehold` does *not* create this link.

12. **AssignOwnerHouseholdSize [M]** — sets `householdSize` = existing owners sharing the `householdId` + 1 (the new owner); minimum 1.

13. **RequireRegistrationDateNotFuture [V]** — if a `registrationDate` was supplied, rejects (`FutureRegistrationDateException`, 400) when it's after the server's current date. Validates the value *as supplied* (before resolution); omitted date is left alone.

14. **ResolveOwnerRegistrationDate [M]** — defaults `registrationDate` to today if absent, then rolls a weekend date forward to the next business day, so the stored date is always a weekday. Everything downstream derives from this adjusted date.

15. **RequireDailyRegistrationCapacity [V]** — rejects (`DailyRegistrationLimitException`, 429) if ≥ 100 owners are already registered on the resolved business-day `registrationDate`.

16. **FlagOwnerBulkSignup [M]** — sets `bulkSignupWarning` = true when more than 80 owners are already registered on that resolved date, else false.

17. **AssignOwnerCustomerCode [M]** — sets `customerCode` = `<REGION>-<HASH8>`, derived from postcode region + a hash of telephone and last name.

18. **AssignOwnerNamesakeCount [M]** — sets `namesakeCount` = count of existing owners with the same first+last name (case-insensitive); computed pre-save so it never counts itself.

19. **FlagOwnerPossibleDuplicate [M]** — soft-duplicate flag: sets `possibleDuplicate` / `possibleDuplicateOf` (lowest matching id) when an existing owner shares last name (case-insensitive) + postcode but has a *different* telephone. A declared household member (`sharesHousehold`) or an owner with no postcode is never flagged. Compares only against already-stored owners.

20. **SaveOwner [P]** — persists the owner via `OwnerRepository.save` (assigns its id).

21. **AuditOwnerCreated [P]** — emits an `AUDIT` log entry with the generated id, customer code, registration date, and derived membership level.

22. **RespondWithOwnerCreated [P]** — maps the saved owner to `OwnerDto` and sends `201 Created` with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

## Notes
- **All-or-nothing:** because every step is under one transaction, any rejection at steps 2–15/16-19 rolls back — though only step 20 writes, so earlier rejections have nothing persisted to undo anyway.
- **Ordering matters and is deliberate:** normalization precedes each of its dependent checks (address→required-fields, telephone→length & identity, email→allowed & identity), and date resolution (14) precedes the daily-capacity (15) and bulk-signup (16) counts so they bucket by the same stored business day.
- There is a `ValidateOwner` class in the codebase, but it is **not** wired into this POST pipeline — bean-validation of the body is not part of create-owner as it currently stands.
